ageing_relevance.rationale: High ageing/senescence literature share, UniProt role in cellular senescence, associations with several age-related diseases, and it is a GrimAge component. Disease association scores are modest, and the GrimAge link is a methylation surrogate, not measured protein.

evidence.value: One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up GrimAge, the mortality clock that was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia in part 1 of this project (an effect explained by smoking). The surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein levels. Shirai et al. 2024 (7-cohort meta-analysis): DNAm-predicted level higher in schizophrenia/first-episode psychosis.

background_knowledge: Human PAI-1 deficiency and mouse models (e.g. Klotho-deficient, Kuro-o) support a pro-ageing role of high PAI-1; the Amish SERPINE1 null mutation is linked to longevity.

mechanism.rationale: Well-characterised inhibitor of tPA/uPA that regulates fibrinolysis and senescence. Lowering activity is the clear direction, although it has several protease-independent roles.

evidence.value: Serine protease inhibitor... primary inhibitor of tissue-type plasminogen activator (PLAT) and urokinase-type plasminogen activator (PLAU)... involved in cellular and replicative senescence

background_knowledge: PAI-1 is a SASP component and drives senescence through p53 signalling.

tractability.rationale: Small-molecule tractability is at the Advanced Clinical level, with a ligand-bound structure and a high-quality pocket. The protein is secreted, so antibodies are feasible. There is no approved drug.

safety.rationale: Two liabilities are listed. Bleeding is the expected on-target risk: the top disease associations include congenital PAI-1 deficiency and abnormal bleeding, which implies bleeding when PAI-1 activity is lost.

evidence.value: congenital plasminogen activator inhibitor type 1 deficiency (0.684), Abnormal bleeding (0.269), hemorrhage (0.16)

clinical_precedence.rationale: Only one drug, aleplasinin, has reached the clinic, and it stopped at Phase 1.

assessment.summary: SERPINE1 (PAI-1) is a secreted inhibitor of tPA/uPA with a documented role in senescence. About 21% of its papers mention ageing, it is associated with cardiovascular, metabolic and neurodegenerative disease, and it is a GrimAge component. Both small-molecule and antibody routes are tractable, but the only clinical candidate, aleplasinin, stopped at Phase 1. The main concern is bleeding from reduced fibrinolytic control. I would inhibit it and recommend consideration, ideally with partial or localised inhibition.
key_uncertainties: Bleeding risk from chronic PAI-1 inhibition in older people
The GrimAge link is a DNA-methylation surrogate, not measured protein, and the schizophrenia effect was explained by smoking
Whether disease associations are causal or reflect biomarker elevation
Protease-independent functions may be affected differently from fibrinolysis
